tier1.text: The axon carries signals away from a neuron, or nerve cell, to other neurons, muscles or glands. A neuron usually has just one axon, which comes out of the cell body, the main part of the neuron. Many axons are wrapped in myelin, a fatty coating that helps signals travel faster. The axon ends in axon terminals, which release chemicals that pass the signal on to other cells.

quotes.quote: An axon is a tube-like structure that propagates the integrated signal to specialized endings called axon terminals. These terminals in turn synapse on other neurons, muscle, or target organs. Chemicals released at axon terminals allow signals to be communicated to these other cells.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.
